citation_details.author: Ziwei Tian, Sha Huang, Bingliang Hu, Li Feng, Quan Wang
citation_details.abstract:
OBJECTIVE
Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is associated with lateralized memory dysfunction, but the dynamic cognitive processes underlying these deficits remain poorly characterized by standard clinical scales. This study investigated whether combining eye-tracking and electroencephalography (EEG) could uncover specific, lateralized patterns of visual exploration and brain activity in LTLE and RTLE patients during a memory task.


METHODS
We enrolled 12 LTLE patients, 18 RTLE patients, and 20 healthy controls (HC), administering Wechsler Memory Scale and a high-load change detection task with synchronized eye-tracking and scalp EEG. We analyzed key eye-tracking metrics (fixation counts, average fixation duration) and event-related potentials reflecting early spatial attention (occipital N1b) and later memory-related activity (temporal late positive component [LPC]).

citation_details.title: Hippocampal interictal spikes disrupt theta-band hippocampal-frontal eye field connectivity: fixation skewness as an indicator of transient network instability
citation_details.author: Ziwei Tian, Sha Huang, Dingyang Liu, Zhiquan Yang, Sushan Li, Bingliang Hu, Li Feng, Quan Wang
citation_details.abstract:
OBJECTIVE
Hippocampal interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) could induce transient visual working memory (VWM) impairments, yet the effect of IEDs on VWM network remain unclear. Since VWM depends on dynamic coordination between memory representations in the hippocampus (HP) and visual exploration controlled by the frontal eye field (FEF), we tested whether hippocampal IEDs disrupt this circuit's functional connectivity and whether such disruption is reflected in altered viewing patterns, offering a behavioral readout of transient network dysfunction.


METHODS
Seven epilepsy patients with hippocampal IEDs and fourteen healthy controls performed a VWM task with eye tracking. In patients, intracranial electroencephalogram (iEEG) was simultaneously recorded from the HP and FEF. We quantified IED-related changes in HP-FEF functional connectivity and examined fixation metrics across IED-related time windows, as well as their relationships with IED counts and task performance.
